description.purpose: The window of one model, owned in one place, with a ledger of every call. The hive decides the whole context of the model it serves -- the system part, the history and the running round -- and writes down, per call, exactly which blocks went out: every element is stored once under the sha256 of its canonical JSON, the wall records the order they arrived in, and `calls` plus `call_blocks` rebuild any request byte for byte. The system part is sent only when a family of it changed, and then as one `$replace` root; between two rebuilds only the end of the window moves, which is what a provider's prefix cache keys on. When the model reports that its cache has gone cold, or the prompt crosses `compress_at` of the context window, a small model of the hive's own condenses the older history into one summary, which the window then carries as `system.history.summary` -- never while a call waits, at most one at a time, and a failed summary leaves the window as it was. Since 1.1.0 ([#892](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/892), [#893](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/893), [#895](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/895), [#896](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/896)) the window follows a role (`role`: `talky`, `consult`, `coding`, `research`), foreign words and tool results stand behind a short id `[#<12 hex>]` the model can release or pin through the `window` section of its answer, another hive can pin a text into the window (`in_pin`), and the hive answers the collector's menu question itself (`./schemas`); `./history` answers the `history_*` tools out of the ledger, `./push` builds the memory leg's question and looks a `gap` up after the answer, and `./handover` hands a new session a note on the last one and a renewed duplex call a block of the recent conversation. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 1.1.1 ([#904](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/904)) the cache clock is one standing order under a fixed id per hive, re-armed on every call (`add` with `rearm`), so the timer keeps one row for it instead of one per call; a repair, so it is the third digit. Since 1.3.0 ([#925](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/925), [#926](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/926), [#931](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/931)) every ledger row carries `audience_set`, the audience of the round that caused it, and every reader serves a row only to a round that lies within it; a history tool called without a round is answered `missing_audience`, the window and the handover of a round-less call take only the running session's rows that declare no round either, a pin without a round is refused, the ledger marks a tool error, a clarifying question and a rewritten standing instruction once each, and `./stats` answers `in_stats` with counts of the hive's own ledger on `stats`. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 1.4.0 ([#932](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/932), [#935](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/935)) every reader selects its rows through the store's `covers` operator, so a round reads only the rows it may see and never learns how many it may not; a row written without a round carries `[]`; `hop.turn_id` counts per round as `<session>#<tag>-<index>`; the knob `identity_budget` (`full` or `split`) decides whether the identity goes whole into every call or whole once and short after it; and the pack takes a fifth family, `identity_short`. A caller can do what it could not before, so it is the second digit. Since 1.4.1 ([#941](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/941)) the model call carries `hop.episode_turn_id`, the id `turn_write` gives the person's episode of that turn, so a reader of a sidecar section can address the episode; no lane moved, so it is the third digit. Since 1.5.0 ([#943](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/943)) `./policy` keeps one window plan per round under its `round_key` rather than one per hive, bounded by the params `max_round_plans` and `round_plan_idle_s`. Params joined, so it is the second digit. Since 1.6.0 ([#949](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/949)) another part of the colony hands the curator candidates on `in_candidate` (acknowledged on `candidate_ack` when asked for), and the live ones a turn covers are pushed into the round's wall within a budget; with `things_section` on, the section `things` leaves as `thing_seen` under the round it was drawn in; and `./reader` answers `in_read` with the turns and sessions the caller's round may see. Lanes joined the boundary, so it is the second digit. Since 1.7.0 ([#972](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/972), [#955](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/955)) a pin carries the round its row proves: `turn_round` and the edge round bound it, a pin no round can prove stays `pin:held`, all audience groups of one source travel in one message, and two first rebuild claims of the same round leave exactly one winner. A caller can rely on what was never promised before, so it is the second digit.
description.use_when: In front of any `llm` cell whose window must not grow without bound or must be accountable: instantiate it with `ctx.model` for its summarizer, send the round on `in_curate`, draw `brain` onto the model with `curator_call`, `session_id`, `turn_id` and `iter` promoted into context, and route every output of the model back on `in_llm` with that context. The model's `system_order` puts `history` after `identity`, `persona` and `instructions`, so the summary is the last and least stable part of the system prompt.
description.not_in_scope: No retrieval and no tool round of its own: the caller gathers, this hive keeps and projects -- the one tool family it answers is the model's own wall (`history_*`). No judgement of what is true: a summary reports what was said. It never parses a sidecar block: the parent's splitter cuts it and hands the curator its own sections (`window`, `gap`, `memory`) on `in_section`.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed; a mutation edge onto a cell inside is refused with hive_port_boundary). Entry: in_curate, in_slots, in_llm, in_pack, in_close, in_model, in_section, in_pin, in_schemas, in_history_call, in_recall_ask, in_gap_bundle, in_renewed, in_stats. Exit on `hop.route`: brain, turn_write, write, pack_ack, model_refused, sidecar, tool_schemas, tool_result, recall, stats.

LEDGER - `blocks` (hash, kind, chars, body, first_seen), `wall` (seq, session_id, turn_id, iter, kind, hash, nth, final, episode_idx, at), `calls`, `call_blocks`, `summaries`, `slots`, `state`, `marks` (seq, session_id, turn_id, kind, value, at), `pins` (hash, source, until, at). A call is rebuilt by reading its `call_blocks` in `pos` order and each block's `body`: the system leaves first, then the messages.

REBUILD - a tap stamped `cache_expires_at` sets the clock (one standing order, re-armed for this call); when it fires for the newest call, the wall between the last summary and the newest `keep_recent` rounds goes to the summarizer with the previous summary, and the next call's `actions` name `rebuild:cache` and the summary id.

ROLE - `./policy` `role` `talky`: today raw, yesterday one summary, older nothing, the newest 40 rounds raw, short ids `[#<12 hex>]` on somebody else's words and tool results; the model's `window` section releases ids (one line from the next rebuild on, `history_read` brings them back) or pins them.

HISTORY - the model reads its own wall (GH #893): `history_search` (phrase, exact or regex, newest first, `#<12 hex>` ids with excerpts), `history_read` (a block by its id or a turn range, whole or refused `too_large`), `history_outline` (sessions and their topics). The parent routes `hop.tool_name` starting `history_` to `in_history_call` and takes `tool_result` into its collector's `in_tool`.

HANDOVER - a closed session leaves a note written by the summarizer off the hot path; the first call of a NEW session carries it as `system.history.handover` with the topic still open (without a close: the topic alone, put together without a model), and a renewed live session of a running call gets the conversation so far -- turns, summary, pins, topic -- as a `sidecar` section `context` at once (GH #896).

model.because: the model the summarizer condenses the history with
